publisher_claims: Internal institutional email is described broadly as all incoming and outgoing email between members; outside-world traffic is excluded.
Each recipient contributes a directed row; four departmental subnetworks are provided.
Time is source-relative seconds beginning at zero; advertised spans are 803 days for the full release and Dept2, and 802 days for Dept3.
Departmental identifiers differ from whole-network identifiers.
limits_for_admission: No interval-specific capture mask or interruption explanation was located on this page.
No participant entry/exit history or absolute calendar mapping was supplied in the inspected description.
A broad publisher scope statement is retained without promoting it to verified per-window coverage.

publisher_claims: The static institutional core has one published department assignment per individual among 42 departments.
The page links provenance to email-EuAll and notes identifier differences.
limits_for_admission: Whole-release department labels are not temporal membership spells.
Cross-release person mapping cannot be inferred from equal identifier values.

publisher_claims: The older collection is described as October 2003 to May 2005, termed 18 months, with 3,038,531 emails.
Its complete-graph claim is scoped to 1,258 institutional addresses.
limits_for_admission: The description does not map the current departmental payload clocks or provide coverage for their exact windows.

sources.title: Motifs in Temporal Networks
publisher_claims: EMAIL-EU has 986 nodes, about 332,000 temporal edges and an 803-day span; event resolution is one second.
Four departmental subnetworks were extracted for motif comparisons.
Unique times simplify the theoretical definition; adaptations can handle ties.
Reference 17 points to the 2007 graph-evolution paper.
limits_for_admission: No departmental calendar transformation, interval observation mask or explanation of the observed empty periods was located in the inspected sections.
The theoretical timing discussion does not establish an order for simultaneous released email rows.

sources.title: Graph Evolution: Densification and Shrinking Diameters
publisher_claims: The older data description covers October 2003 to May 2005 and scopes complete institutional communication to 1,258 addresses.
Its graph analysis requires reciprocal exchange and also considers two-month sliding windows.
It describes the institutional core as largely stable.
limits_for_admission: The reciprocal graph and older collection description are not interchangeable with current directed departmental record payloads.
A largely stable core is not an individual presence history or exact release mapping.

publisher_claims: The project links the temporal email release and reports its 803-day span.
limits_for_admission: No coverage supplement, timestamp transformation or gap explanation was located on the inspected page.

publisher_claims: The linked BSD terms concern software source and binary redistribution.
limits_for_admission: These software terms are not transferred to the raw email dataset; no dataset-specific grant was stated on the reviewed primary pages.

unresolved_provenance.interpretation: Related provenance does not establish exact calendar mapping or identify which description should govern the current payload.

observation_decision.reason: Inspected sources do not provide the exact release, participant, interval and observation evidence required by strict R1.
